fine_trace.code: if (a > 0xff) { gen_B(s, OP_EXT1); gen_B(s, i); gen_S(s, a); pos = s->pc; gen_S(s, pc); }
fine_trace.note: When the register operand a exceeds 0xff, genjmp2 emits the jump destination by calling gen_S(s, pc) directly, writing the absolute position pc (a uint32_t truncated to 16 bits) into the destination field instead of the relative offset pc - pos2 that gen_jmpdst would compute.
dispatch reads the 16-bit destination field at pos0. Because genjmp2 wrote the absolute position pc (not an offset), newpos equals that absolute position value.
dispatch returns pos1+newpos = (pos0+2)+pc. Since pc is an absolute position rather than a relative offset, this computed next position can point far beyond the current iseq buffer.
dispatch_linked feeds the returned pos1+newpos back into dispatch. If that value lands at the last byte of the heap buffer (pos0 == icapa-1), the next PEEK_S(s->iseq+pos0) reads 1 byte out of bounds.
The 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read occurs here: PEEK_S reads (pc)[0] and (pc)[1], and when pos0 == icapa-1 the second byte is beyond the allocated iseq buffer.
